senses.definition: simple past and past participle of bind
examples: I bound the splint to my leg.
I had bound the splint with duct tape.

senses.definition: (linguistics, of a morpheme) That cannot stand alone as a free word.
(mathematics, logic, of a variable) Constrained by a quantifier.
(dated) Constipated; costive.
(in combination) Confined or restricted to a certain place.
(in combination) Unable to move in certain conditions.

examples: Which way are you bound? —I'm already homeward bound.

examples: They were bound to come into conflict eventually.

senses.definition: (often used in plural) A boundary, the border which one must cross in order to enter or leave a territory.
examples: I reached the northern bound of my property, took a deep breath and walked on.
Somewhere within these bounds you may find a buried treasure.
